chapter: Barnet, 52nd Street and New York recording dates
title: His own small bands on 52nd Street and in Chicago
summary: His band had Dexter Gordon, Curly Russell, Denzil Best and Jimmy Jones, and a later group of Washington players at Chicago's Capitol Lounge.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Whom did you have in your band?
Well, I told you last night, one band I had -- I had Dexter Gordon, Curly Russell and Denzil Best on drums, Jimmy Jones was on piano. Guess that was about it, about five of us, small band.

Only on 52nd Street. The Downbeat, you know, almost -- that's the spot, only place to work around New York at that particular time, and I brought a band from -- I picked up another band in Washington, some guys, and I went to Chicago, and I told you this too the other night, and that was John Malachi and Tommy Potter and -- who the heck else was on that band there? Marlo Morris was on piano. I don't know if you ever heard of him, but he played good.
Hey done a lot of records.
Yeah, I had guys like that in the band, you know. But three of the guys I picked up in Washington,

was Harry Curtis, alto saxophone -- four guys -- John Malachi, Tommy Potter and Leo Williamson, tenor man. I picked them up in Washington, and I put a couple guys with that band. I went up to Chicago, and I played for about three months at the Capitol Lounge right next to the Chicago Theater, in a little place right on the (inaudible) alley. I think I mentioned that.

Yeah, I didn't remember the name of the hotel. It was -- this was when I played with Earl, though. It's right on the corner from the Grand Terrace. I didn't remember that name, but Lawrence Brown, all of them, they stayed at this hotel, lot of guys. I couldn't remember the name of it. I don't know if they call it the South Parkway Hotel or what hotel, but it was right on the corner.
